reason: The text is the conquest narrative of Jericho (Joshua 6) and depicts the Israelites experiencing divine military victory, not suffering. Joshua conveys God's instructions for the assault and warns the people against violating the sacred ban (herem) on plunder. The narrative shows leadership providing tactical and religious guidance within the context of promised success, not leaders assigning blame to a suffering people. There is no portrayal of the Hebrew people suffering greatly or leaders attributing their circumstances to their fault.
